variants.neutral: Mira reaches the empty platform as rain drums on the tin roof; the departure board says the last train leaves in an hour.
variants.happy: Mira hops over a puddle onto the platform, laughing at how loud the rain is on the tin roof; the last train is still an hour away.
variants.uplift: Mira's heart races as she reaches the platform; the board glows through the rain and the last train leaves in just an hour.
variants.sad: Mira stands alone on the platform, rain streaming off the roof, watching the board count down the last hour before the final train.

variants.neutral: A sleepy clerk slides a ticket under the glass without looking up; the office smells of old paper and coffee.
variants.happy: The clerk winks and slides Mira a ticket along with a paper cup of coffee, still warm.
variants.uplift: The clerk startles awake, then grins and rushes the ticket through the glass as if the whole station were running late.
variants.sad: The clerk hands over the ticket with a tired nod; neither of them says anything, and the clock ticks loudly.

variants.neutral: In the waiting room an old woman pours tea from a dented thermos and offers the spare cup to Mira.
variants.happy: The old woman beams and presses a steaming cup into Mira's hands; they trade silly stories until the cup is empty.
variants.uplift: The old woman's tales of past storms make Mira lean in, wide-eyed, forgetting the cold entirely.
variants.sad: The old woman pours tea and says nothing; the quiet is gentle, and Mira's shoulders slowly relax.

variants.neutral: Behind a wire cage, shelves of forgotten umbrellas and suitcases wait; one small brass key lies on the counter.
variants.happy: Mira finds a brass key tucked inside an umbrella and giggles at the thought of what it might open.
variants.uplift: A brass key gleams among the lost things, and Mira's pulse jumps; surely it opens something important.
variants.sad: Among the forgotten umbrellas lies a lonely brass key; Mira turns it over, wondering who lost it.

variants.neutral: On the iron footbridge the wind pulls at Mira's coat; below, the rails shine like wet ribbons in the dark.
variants.happy: Mira grins into the wind on the footbridge, the rails below shining like ribbons she could dance along.
variants.uplift: The wind whips across the footbridge and Mira feels alive, the whole dark station spread out beneath her.
variants.sad: Mira holds the cold rail of the footbridge and watches the rails vanish into the dark, small and quiet.

callbacks.text: The tea's warmth lingers in her hands against the wind.

variants.neutral: The signal room hums with old relays and a cage of heavy levers; a faded sign says the points must be set before the train arrives.
variants.happy: Mira pats the levers like old friends; the whole signal room hums as if it were glad of company.
variants.uplift: Relays click and the levers shudder; Mira knows the points must be set before the train comes, and time is short.
variants.sad: The signal room is cold and humming; Mira reads the faded sign and feels how much depends on a few heavy levers.

callbacks.text: The brass key turns in the lever cage as though it had always belonged there.

variants.neutral: A storm slams the platform; the lamps swing wildly and Mira shields her face as she crosses to the waiting rails.
variants.happy: Rain hammers down and Mira whoops into the storm, soaked and delighted as the lamps swing overhead.
variants.uplift: Lightning cracks above the station and Mira runs the length of the platform, heart pounding, toward the distant headlight.
variants.sad: The storm drives everyone indoors; Mira walks on alone, collar up, steady in the noise toward the rails.

variants.neutral: The last train sighs into the station, its windows glowing gold; Mira climbs aboard and the doors close behind her.
variants.happy: The last train glides in like a lit-up lantern and Mira bounds aboard, smiling as the doors seal out the rain.
variants.uplift: Brakes shriek and the last train bursts into the station; Mira leaps aboard just as the doors begin to close.
variants.sad: The last train arrives quietly, its windows warm; Mira steps aboard, finds a seat, and lets the doors close on the night.

callbacks.text: The ticket from the clerk is still crisp in her pocket.
Through the window she sees the old woman wave from the waiting room.

endings.text: The train pulls out and Mira watches the station glow behind her, warmer than the night had any right to be; she will remember this one fondly.
Mira's pulse is still racing as the lights slide past; she grins at her reflection, already wondering what the next night train might hold.
Mira rests her head against the cool window as the rain softens; the night was heavy, but the rhythm of the rails is steadying.
The train hums into the dark and Mira settles in; the night was ordinary and strange in equal measure, and she is content to let it go.
